title: Unbounded direct-image truncation stability from local bounds
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with commutative ring sheaves on sites small relative to the module-sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories and cohomology $H^j$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal A\subset\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal B\subset\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ be weak Serre subcategories, meaning strictly full subcategories containing zero and closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between their objects and under extensions. Write $D_{\mathcal A}$ and $D_{\mathcal B}$ for the full subcategories with all cohomology in these subcategories, and $D^+_{\mathcal A}$ and $D^+_{\mathcal B}$ for their bounded-below parts (cohomology zero in all degrees below some integer). A triple $(\mathcal E,S,\mathcal H)$ has the local bound property if there is a set $\mathcal V\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal E)$ such that every site object has a covering by members of $\mathcal V$, and each $V\in\mathcal V$ admits an integer $d_V$ and a cofinal collection of covering families $\{V_i\to V\}$ such that $H^p(V_i,F)=0$ for $p>d_V$ and all $F\in\mathcal H$. Cofinal means that every covering family has a refinement in this collection; $H^p(V_i,F)$ is right derived sections of $F$. Suppose both $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O,\mathcal A)$ and $(\mathcal D,R,\mathcal B)$ have this property. Let $N\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $R^pf_*F\in\mathcal B$ for all $F\in\mathcal A$ and $p\geq0$, and $R^pf_*F=0$ for all $p>N$. For total derived direct image $Rf_*$, computed by K-injective resolutions, every $K\in D_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal O)$ has $Rf_*K\in D_{\mathcal B}(R)$. For every $n\geq0$ and $j\geq N-n$, the map induced by good truncation $K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K$ [def-kun-truncations] gives an isomorphism
$$H^j(Rf_*K)\longrightarrow H^j(Rf_*(\tau_{\geq-n}K)).$$
No flatness or equivalence hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text:
Put $T_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$ and $L_n=Rf_*T_n$. Good truncation retains $H^q(K)$ for $q\geq-n$ and gives zero below, so $T_n\in D^+_{\mathcal A}$. Module categories on these small ringed sites are Grothendieck and admit K-injective resolutions. Module direct image is additive by its definition. Its underlying sheaf functor is a right adjoint, so it preserves the equalizer defining a kernel: transpose an equalizing map by the sheaf adjunction, factor it uniquely through the kernel, and transpose back. The factor is module-linear because the module operations are induced by that same adjunction. Thus module direct image preserves kernels and is left exact. The bounded-below hypercohomology spectral sequence therefore gives
$$E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*H^q(T_n)\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(L_n),\qquad p\geq0,\ q\geq-n.$$
Each $E_2$ term lies in $\mathcal B$. Successive pages are kernels modulo images of maps between such objects, hence remain in $\mathcal B$ by weak Serre closure; in each total degree the finite filtration supplied by convergence has these stable terms as its graded pieces. Repeated extension closure puts its abutment in $\mathcal B$. Also no term has total degree below $-n$. Consequently $L_n\in D^+_{\mathcal B}$.

proof.text:
For an integer $r\geq1$, the successive lower-truncation triangle is
$$H^{-r}(K)[r]\longrightarrow T_r\longrightarrow T_{r-1}\longrightarrow H^{-r}(K)[r+1].$$
Apply the triangulated $Rf_*$ and the long exact cohomology sequence. The shifted-single identification gives $H^a(Rf_*(H^{-r}(K)[r]))=R^{a+r}f_*H^{-r}(K)$ when $a+r\geq0$, and zero when $a+r<0$. In particular this group is zero whenever $a+r>N$: use the given higher-image bound in nonnegative degrees, and the negative-degree vanishing otherwise. Fix $n\geq0$ and $j\geq N-n$. For every $r\geq n+1$, both $j+r$ and $j+1+r$ exceed $N$. Thus the two outer groups in
$$H^j(Rf_*(H^{-r}K[r]))\to H^j(L_r)\to H^j(L_{r-1})\to H^{j+1}(Rf_*(H^{-r}K[r]))$$
are zero. Exactness makes the middle map an isomorphism. Finite composition proves $H^j(L_m)\to H^j(L_n)$ is an isomorphism for all $m\geq n$ and $j\geq N-n$. This includes the boundary $j=N-n$.

source.place: Tag 0D6U, proof: comparison between lower truncations, expanded using successive-truncation triangles

proof.text:
Apply the source-site reconstruction theorem to $K$ with the given local bound property for $\mathcal A$. It identifies the canonical maps with an isomorphism $K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_nT_n$. Represent $K$ by a complex and use its good truncations as a strict tower. Apply the ringed-topos pushforward–limit comparison to this tower (reindex $n\geq0$ by $n+1\geq1$). It gives
$$Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_nL_n.$$
The comparison commutes with every projection, so the composite to $L_n$ is precisely $Rf_*$ applied to $K\to T_n$. No exactness of module pullback or of countable products is needed.

proof.text: For each $j$, choose $n_j=\max(0,N-j)$. Step 2 says every transition of $(H^j(L_n))$ at index at least $n_j$ is an isomorphism. Step 1 puts all $L_n$ in $D^+_{\mathcal B}$, so the target-site stationary-limit theorem applies with the given local bound property for $\mathcal B$. It identifies the canonical projection $H^j(R\varprojlim_mL_m)\to H^j(L_n)$ as an isomorphism whenever $n\geq n_j$. These sheaves lie in $\mathcal B$, so the limit has all cohomology in $\mathcal B$. With step 3 this proves $Rf_*K\in D_{\mathcal B}$. Finally, if $n\geq0$ and $j\geq N-n$, then $n\geq\max(0,N-j)=n_j$. The same projection, identified in step 3 with the canonical truncation map, proves exactly the required isomorphism.
